genealogy.paternal_divine: God the Father — eternal begetting, not created (John 1:1–3; Colossians 1:15–17)
genealogy.maternal_human: Mary of Nazareth, of the lineage of David through Joseph (legal), Luke 3 traces line through Mary to Adam
genealogy.davidic_line: Matthew 1:1–17 traces legal genealogy through Joseph: Abraham → David → Solomon → Josiah → Zerubbabel → Joseph
genealogy.lucan_line: Luke 3:23–38 traces through Nathan son of David → Heli → Adam → God (biological/Marian line per many interpreters)
genealogy.significance: The two genealogies establish both royal legal claim (Matthew: Joseph/kingly line) and biological humanity (Luke: to Adam, affirming full humanity). Christ fulfills Davidic covenant (2 Samuel 7:12–16) as eternal king.

biblical_angel.name: Jesus Christ — The Logos Incarnate
biblical_angel.rank: Son of God / Second Person of the Trinity
biblical_angel.canonical_function: Eternal Son and Logos (Word) through whom all things were created (John 1:1–3; Col 1:16–17). Incarnated as fully human and fully divine. Crucified, died, buried, resurrected on the third day. Ascended to the right hand of the Father. Will return as Judge of the living and dead (Nicene Creed, 381 CE).
source_texts: Colossians 1:15–20 (Firstborn over all creation, all things created through and for him)
Hebrews 1:1–4 (Heir of all things, through whom the universe was made)
Philippians 2:5–11 (Kenosis — emptying of divine prerogatives in incarnation)

kabbalistic.angelic_order: Central node of the Tree of Life — the divine mediator between Kether and Malkuth
source_texts: Christian Kabbalah — Pico della Mirandola Conclusiones (1486)

hermetic.role: The incarnate Logos — divine reason and creative intelligence made flesh; the ultimate expression of 'as above so below' in that the infinite condescends into the finite
hermetic.corpus_hermeticum_ref: Structural parallel to the Nous (divine intellect) that illuminates the fallen soul; Hermetic prisca theologia traditions (Ficino, Agrippa) placed Christ at the apex of the ancient wisdom lineage
hermetic.agrippan_attribution: Agrippa, Three Books of Occult Philosophy III.36 — Christ as the supreme name above all names

gnostic.name: Christos / The Savior / Logos
source_texts: Gospel of Thomas (Nag Hammadi NHC II.2) — sayings tradition
Gospel of Philip (NHC II.3) — sacramental theology
Pistis Sophia — Christ as revealer of hidden light
Valentinian Gospel of Truth — Christ as teacher who reveals the Father

islamic.quranic_reference: Quran 3:45–47 (Annunciation); 4:171 (Word of God, Spirit from Him); 5:110 (miracles); 19:16–34 (Nativity); 43:61 (sign of the Hour)
islamic.isra_iliyyat_link: Islamic tradition affirms virgin birth, miracles, ascension; denies crucifixion-death (4:157). ʿĪsā is Word of God (kalimatu'Llāh) and Spirit from Him (rūḥun minhu) — titles unique in the Quran.

planetary.agrippa_book_ref: Agrippa OCPhil III.36 — the Name of Christ above all magical names

functional_domains: Fulfillment of Mosaic Law and Prophets
Cosmic Creatorship (all things made through him)

relationships.notes: Michael serves as commander of the heavenly host under Christ's ultimate lordship. Some patristic writers (Origen, some modern scholars) have proposed Michael-Christ identification, but mainstream orthodoxy holds them distinct.
Gabriel is sent by God to announce Christ's birth to Mary — the Annunciation. Gabriel's role as divine messenger is fulfilled most climactically in the Incarnation announcement.

relationships.source_text: 3 Enoch; Christian Kabbalistic syncretic sources (Pico, Reuchlin)
relationships.notes: Both Metatron and Christ serve as supreme mediators between the divine throne and humanity. Christian Kabbalists explicitly mapped Christ onto Metatron's role. The parallel is typological, not doctrinal in mainstream Christianity.

relationships.source_text: Frazer, The Golden Bough (1890); modern nuanced treatments in Assmann, Hornung
relationships.notes: Both involve death, resurrection motif, judgment of the dead, and divine kingship. Scholars emphasize fundamental differences: Osiris undergoes physical reassembly, Christ's resurrection is bodily glorification. The parallel is structural and comparative, not historical derivation.

relationships.source_text: Ficino, Theologia Platonica; Agrippa OCPhil III
relationships.notes: Renaissance Christian Hermeticists placed Christ as the apex of the prisca theologia lineage, with Hermes Trismegistus as a prophetic anticipation of the Logos. Ficino saw Hermeticism as preparation for Christian revelation.

relationships.source_text: Revelation 22:16 (Christ calls himself the 'bright morning star'); Isaiah 14:12 (Lucifer/Helel)
relationships.notes: Christ claims the title 'Morning Star' in Revelation 22:16, the same astronomical image used in Isaiah 14:12 for 'Helel ben Shahar.' This creates a deliberate typological inversion: what Satan usurped, Christ legitimately holds. The identification is antithetical, not equivalence.

entities.research_notes: In this concordance, Jesus Christ occupies the theological center: Colossians 1:16–17 states explicitly that 'all things were created through him and for him... and in him all things hold together.' This is not a claim about one deity among many, but the claim that the Logos is the ontological ground of all that exists — including all the figures mapped in this database. Every tradition vector mapped here can be read through this lens: pagan deities as corrupted or partial perceptions of the same reality; angelic orders as servants of the same sovereign; esoteric traditions as groping toward what Christ revealed plainly. The genealogies of Matthew and Luke establish his historical particularity — the Logos became flesh at a specific time, in a specific lineage, in a specific place. This guards against pure abstraction.

biblical_angel.name: Metatron
biblical_angel.canonical_function: Heavenly scribe, divine chancellor, angel of the presence

enochian.name: Enoch
enochian.sin_or_role: Translated to heaven without death; became Metatron

hermetic.role: Revealer of divine wisdom; author of Hermetic corpus
hermetic.agrippan_attribution: Rules over all writing, magic, and hidden knowledge

islamic.isra_iliyyat_link: Identified with Enoch in classical Islamic scholarship (al-Tabari, al-Tha'labi)

relationships.source_text: Herodotus Histories II.67; Iamblichus De Mysteriis VIII
relationships.notes: One of the most well-attested ancient syncretisms
Enoch's apotheosis into Metatron maps the Hermetic sage into the angelic hierarchy
Identification is strong in Islamic scholarship but not universal

relationships.source_text: Typological and Logos parallels noted by Christian Hermeticists
relationships.notes: Hermes Trismegistus functions as a wisdom revealer and divine Logos-parallel in some comparative traditions.

entities.research_notes: The figure of Hermes Trismegistus is itself a synthesis — the Hermetic texts were likely composed in Egypt 1st–3rd century CE, blending Platonic philosophy with Egyptian priestly wisdom attributed to Thoth.

enochian.name: Azazel
enochian.sin_or_role: Taught humanity metalworking, weapons, cosmetics, and sorcery. Bound under desert of Dudael until final judgment.

relationships.source_text: Forsyth The Old Enemy (1987); Hanegraaff Fallen Angels (2010)
relationships.notes: Structural parallel — both transmit forbidden technology and are punished. Not claimed by any ancient source.
Azazel is among the 200 Watchers; his sin is treated as more corrupting than Semjaza's
Some traditions conflate; treated as distinct entities here per primary Enochian text

entities.research_notes: The Leviticus 'Azazel' may be a place-name, a function, or a proper demon name — heavily contested. See Stökl Ben Ezra (2003) for the definitive treatment.

egyptian.name: Thoth
egyptian.ennead_position: Scribe and Vizier of Ra; arbiter of the gods

hermetic.role: Divine origin of all Hermetic wisdom

relationships.notes: Foundation of all Hermetic tradition
Both present at the Weighing of the Heart; Thoth records, Anubis guides

relationships.source_text: Studies on sacred scribal Logos figures
relationships.notes: Thoth as divine scribe parallels Logos/Christic functions in typological comparisons.

entities.research_notes: Thoth's association with the moon and lunar calendar distinguishes him from Hermes' solar-mercurial qualities. The syncretism is functional, not cosmological.

biblical_angel.name: Helel ben Shahar
biblical_angel.canonical_function: Taunt-poem figure; later tradition developed into fallen angel

enochian.name: Gadreel / Shemihaza tradition
enochian.sin_or_role: Some traditions link the Light-Bringer motif to Gadreel who led Eve astray

gnostic.name: Sophia (Lower Aspect) / Yaldabaoth (pride parallel)
source_texts: On the Origin of the World

relationships.notes: Conflation common in later Christian demonology; primary sources treat separately
Both represent misappropriation of divine light; structural not claimed parallel
Fire-bringer parallel widely noted by scholars

entities.research_notes: Isaiah 14:12 is a taunt directed at the King of Babylon; the 'fallen angel' interpretation is entirely a later Christian development, not present in the Hebrew text. The Latin 'Lucifer' simply means 'morning star.'

biblical_angel.name: Beelzebub (Patristic identification)
biblical_angel.canonical_function: Patristic demonology identified Baal/Zeus as Beelzebub, Lord of Flies

gnostic.name: Yaldabaoth / Demiurge parallel
gnostic.notes: Gnostic systems often map the chief Archon onto the sky-god of competing traditions

relationships.source_text: Philo of Byblos Phoenician History (via Eusebius)
relationships.notes: Ba'al Hadad and Zeus were formally identified throughout the Hellenistic Near East
Both divine kings; Plutarch himself explores the comparison

entities.research_notes: The Patristic identification of Zeus/Jupiter with demonic forces (Beelzebub, etc.) is a polemical move documented extensively from Justin Martyr onward and is tagged POLEMIC_EQUIVALENT in all edges.

hermetic.role: World-Soul in its chthonic aspect; guardian of thresholds

relationships.notes: Both rule the nocturnal feminine, crossroads, and sorcery; identification made in early modern occultism
In the magical papyri Hecate and Isis are frequently invoked as the same goddess

entities.research_notes: Hesiod grants Hecate unusual prominence for a pre-Olympian figure, giving her dominion over earth, sea, and sky. Her triple-form iconography likely postdates Hesiod.

biblical_angel.name: Michael
biblical_angel.canonical_function: Warrior archangel, protector of Israel, commander of divine armies

enochian.name: Michael
enochian.sin_or_role: One of the four presences before God; binds Azazel and Semjaza

hermetic.role: Solar warrior principle; guardian against adverse forces

islamic.isra_iliyyat_link: One of the four cardinal angels; rules over rain and sustenance in Islamic angelology

relationships.notes: Both function as chief angelic intercessors; different traditions give the prime position to each

relationships.source_text: Assmann Egyptian Theology; Hornung Conceptions of God
relationships.notes: Both are divine warrior sons who battle the embodiment of chaos (Set / Satan)

entities.research_notes: Michael's role expands significantly from the Hebrew Bible through Enochian literature and into Christian angelology. His identification as 'prince of the host' is established in Daniel; his warrior role against Satan is Revelation.

egyptian.name: Osiris
egyptian.ennead_position: Son of Geb and Nut; Husband of Isis; Father of Horus; Lord of the Dead

relationships.source_text: Herodotus II.42; Plutarch De Iside et Osiride ch. 13
relationships.notes: Plutarch explicitly identifies them as aspects of the same divine principle
Horus as son and avenger of Osiris is one of the core Egyptian mythological relationships
Osiris is often compared structurally to savior/resurrection motifs found in Christian tradition; parallels are comparative, not identity claims.

entities.research_notes: Osiris is among the most cosmologically complex Egyptian deities — solar deity, grain deity, and chthonic judge simultaneously. The dying-and-rising god parallel to Christ was a central argument in early 20th century comparative religion (Fraser), now treated with more nuance.

biblical_angel.name: Lilit
biblical_angel.canonical_function: Night creature; appears once in Isaiah 34:14 as wilderness demon

enochian.name: Naamah (related tradition)
enochian.sin_or_role: Naamah identified in some Kabbalistic texts as one of the Watcher-brides; associated with Lilith as dual night-queens

kabbalistic.qliphoth_counterpart: Lilith / Nahemah (Lilith IS the Qliphah of Malkuth)
source_texts: Treatise on the Left Emanation (Kabbalist Isaac ben Jacob ha-Kohen)

hermetic.role: Nocturnal feminine force; embodiment of unbound female power

relationships.notes: Both rule nocturnal feminine power and witchcraft; identification made explicitly in early modern occultism

relationships.source_text: Black The Literature of Ancient Sumer
relationships.notes: Possible Mesopotamian origin of Lilith figure debated; Ereshkigal as dark-feminine archetype parallel

entities.research_notes: Lilith as 'first wife of Adam' is medieval legend, not biblical — originating in the Alphabet of Ben Sira (7th–10th century CE). Her Babylonian antecedent Ardat Lili is debated. The Kabbalistic Lilith is the most developed form.

biblical_angel.name: Metatron
biblical_angel.canonical_function: Highest-ranking angel; chancellor of heaven; sits on a throne beside God (controversial)

enochian.name: Enoch-Metatron
enochian.sin_or_role: Enoch translated alive into heaven, transformed into fiery angel Metatron

hermetic.role: The Nous made personal; divine intellect as angelic being

functional_domains: Transformation of the Human into the Divine

relationships.notes: Both are human sages translated to divine status as celestial scribes
Rival traditions give primacy to each as chief of the heavenly court

relationships.source_text: Christian mystical and Kabbalistic syncretic sources
relationships.notes: Metatron and Christ are both mediating, salvific figures in differing traditions; comparison is typological and not doctrinal.

entities.research_notes: Metatron's name is etymologically disputed: possibly from Greek 'meta thronon' (beside the throne), Latin 'metator' (one who marks out), or the Aramaic 'matron.' His near-divine status caused rabbinic controversy — the heretic Elisha ben Abuya saw him enthroned and concluded 'there are two powers in heaven.'

relationships.source_text: McLean The Goetia of Dr. Rudd (2007)
relationships.notes: Paimon's role as king of universal knowledge parallels the Jovian-solar sovereign archetype

entities.research_notes: Paimon is described as riding a dromedary, crowned, with a fierce countenance, accompanied by two lesser kings Bebal and Abalam. His appearance facing west distinguishes him. The 200 legions figure is among the largest in the Goetia.

biblical_angel.name: Asmodeus
biblical_angel.canonical_function: Demon of lust; slays seven husbands of Sarah; bound by Raphael

enochian.name: Related to Gadreel / Lust-teaching Watchers
enochian.sin_or_role: Connection to Watcher tradition of carnal sin and forbidden knowledge

kabbalistic.angelic_order: Fallen from Seraphim or Thrones class

hermetic.role: Represents unbridled desire opposing the ordered cosmos

relationships.notes: Raphael binds Asmodeus in Egypt — one of the few named angel-demon direct confrontations in canonical-adjacent scripture

entities.research_notes: Asmodeus is one of the most attested demonic figures, appearing in the Book of Tobit, the Talmud (where he is said to have sat on Solomon's throne), and the Goetia. His Zoroastrian cognate Aēšma-daēva (demon of wrath) is the probable origin.

greek.name: Apollo (partial)
source_texts: Plutarch De Iside et Osiride ch. 12

egyptian.name: Horus
egyptian.ennead_position: Son of Osiris and Isis; divine king; Eye of Ra

functional_domains: Vengeance and Justice for the Father

relationships.notes: Son and avenger of Osiris; their myth is central to Egyptian kingship theology
Both are divine sons who battle the cosmic adversary (Set / Satan / Dragon)

source_attestations: Contending of Horus and Seth (Papyrus Chester Beatty I)
entities.research_notes: There are multiple distinct Horus figures in Egyptian tradition: Horus the Elder (Haroeris), brother of Osiris; and Horus the Younger (Harsiese), son of Osiris and Isis. Later tradition merged them. The 'Eye of Horus' is distinct from the 'Eye of Ra.'

biblical_angel.name: Gabriel
biblical_angel.canonical_function: Divine messenger; interpreter of visions; announces births (John the Baptist, Jesus)

enochian.name: Gabriel
enochian.sin_or_role: One of the four presences before God; sent to destroy the giants

hermetic.role: Lunar messenger; bridge between divine and human realms

islamic.isra_iliyyat_link: Transmits divine revelation to Muhammad; identified as the Holy Spirit in some classical Islamic scholarship

relationships.notes: Both are divine messengers between the supreme and the human; Gabriel holds the Abrahamic role Hermes holds in Hellenic tradition

entities.research_notes: Gabriel is among the most cross-traditional of all named angels — appearing in Hebrew Bible, New Testament, Enochian literature, and Quran with consistent messenger function. His Quranic role (transmitting revelation to Muhammad) is his most exalted.

egyptian.name: Hathor / Isis (partial)
egyptian.ennead_position: Hathor as divine beauty and love

relationships.source_text: Plutarch De Iside et Osiride; PGM IV
relationships.notes: Isis absorbed many Aphrodite attributes in the Hellenistic period; both rule love, magic, and the sea

entities.research_notes: The two Aphrodites — Urania (heavenly, spiritual love) and Pandemos (earthly, physical love) — originate in Plato's Symposium (180c–185c) and became a standard distinction in Neoplatonic and Renaissance treatments.

biblical_angel.name: Belial
biblical_angel.canonical_function: Embodiment of worthlessness and wickedness; adversarial force

enochian.name: Belial
enochian.sin_or_role: In DSS War Scroll: Prince of Darkness ruling the forces of evil opposing the Sons of Light

relationships.notes: Paul uses 'Beliar' as near-equivalent to Satan; later tradition sometimes identifies, sometimes separates

entities.research_notes: 'Beli ya'al' is a Hebrew compound meaning 'without worth' or 'without going up (to God).' In the Dead Sea Scrolls, Belial is a fully developed supernatural Prince of Darkness opposing the archangel Michael — the most developed pre-Christian angelological dualism.

greek.name: Hermes Chthonios / Hermes Psychopompos
source_texts: Plutarch De Iside et Osiride ch. 15

egyptian.name: Anubis
egyptian.ennead_position: Son of Osiris (or Ra); god of embalming; conductor of souls to judgment

relationships.notes: Both present at the Weighing of the Heart — Anubis manages the scales, Thoth records the result

relationships.source_text: Plutarch De Iside ch. 15; Apuleius Metamorphoses XI
relationships.notes: Anubis-Hermes syncretism attested in multiple Greco-Roman texts

entities.research_notes: Anubis lost his prominence as lord of the dead to Osiris over the course of Egyptian religious history; by the Middle Kingdom, Osiris is the supreme lord of the Duat and Anubis serves him. His role as embalmer and psychopomp remained constant.

egyptian.name: Geb (earth-time parallel)
egyptian.ennead_position: Father of Osiris, Isis, Set, Nephthys

hermetic.role: Principle of limitation, form, and time; necessary for manifestation

relationships.notes: Zeus overthrows Kronos; the generational conflict is the central Greek cosmogonic myth
Both are demiurgic father-gods who are ultimately displaced; Gnostic systems likely drew on this Titanic model

entities.research_notes: The Greek Kronos / Roman Saturn split is more complex than simple direct correspondence — Saturn had a distinct Italian agricultural prehistory. Their merger was so complete that Saturn's festival (Saturnalia) was the most popular Roman holiday.

egyptian.name: Isis
egyptian.ennead_position: Daughter of Geb and Nut; wife and restorer of Osiris; mother of Horus; supreme magician

hermetic.role: World-Soul in its redemptive, loving aspect; guardian of the body of Osiris (divine knowledge)

relationships.notes: In the Hellenistic world, Isis absorbed nearly every major goddess attribute; Aphrodite identification particularly strong in magical papyri
Isis and Osiris are the divine couple; she is the restorer, he the restored; their myth underlies all Egyptian resurrection theology

entities.research_notes: Isis became the most universally worshipped deity of the Roman Empire by the 1st–3rd centuries CE — her cult spread to Britain, Germany, and the Rhine frontier. Apuleius' Metamorphoses Book XI is the most literary treatment of her mysteries.

enochian.name: Semjaza
enochian.sin_or_role: Led the 200 Watchers in their descent to Mount Hermon; fathered Nephilim; bound until the Day of Judgment hanging between heaven and earth as the constellation Orion in some traditions

relationships.notes: Semjaza is the named leader; Azazel's transgressions are treated as more severe in 1 Enoch 10
Some traditions conflate the Watcher rebellion with Lucifer's fall; 1 Enoch treats them as distinct events

entities.research_notes: The Semjaza narrative in 1 Enoch is almost certainly a reinterpretation of Genesis 6:1–4. His name may derive from Aramaic 'shem' (name) + 'azza' (strong/daring) — 'he who dares the Name of God.' The constellation identification (Orion) appears in later midrashic tradition.

genealogy.origin: Formed from dust of the ground (adamah), breath of life from God (Genesis 2:7)
genealogy.lineage: Genesis 5 — Adam → Seth → Enosh → Kenan → Mahalalel → Jared → Enoch → Methuselah → Lamech → Noah
genealogy.to_christ: Luke 3:38 terminates the Lucan genealogy of Jesus at 'the son of Adam, the son of God' — connecting Christ's humanity to the first man and through him to God

biblical_angel.name: Adam
biblical_angel.canonical_function: Created in the image of God (imago Dei — Genesis 1:26–27); federal head of humanity; through his disobedience sin entered the world (Romans 5:12); typological counterpart to Christ as 'Last Adam' (1 Corinthians 15:45–49)

kabbalistic.angelic_order: Adam Kadmon — the Primordial Human of Lurianic Kabbalah; template for the divine anthropomorphic form
source_texts: Lurianic Kabbalah — Etz Chaim on Adam Kadmon

gnostic.name: Adam / Adamas (Heavenly Adam)
source_texts: Apocryphon of John NHC II.1 — Yaldabaoth creates earthly Adam but divine spark placed within him
Gospel of the Egyptians — Adamas as heavenly archetype

hermetic.role: Primordial Man (Anthropos) who descended into matter; prototype of the soul's fall and potential return
hermetic.corpus_hermeticum_ref: Corpus Hermeticum I (Poimandres) — the Anthropos who fell in love with Nature and became entangled in matter

islamic.quranic_reference: Quran 2:30–39; 7:11–25; 20:115–123 — first prophet; angels commanded to bow; Satan's refusal begins his enmity
islamic.isra_iliyyat_link: Islamic tradition preserves full Garden narrative; Adam and Eve's descent to earth frames all subsequent prophecy. Adam is first of the prophetic chain culminating in Muhammad.

relationships.notes: Paul's Adam-Christ typology: 'As in Adam all die, so in Christ all will be made alive' (1 Cor 15:22). Adam is the type, Christ is the antitype — the Last Adam who undoes what the first Adam broke. This is one of the most structurally significant theological relationships in the database.
The Watcher descent into human women connects to Adam's line — the Nephilim are descendants of unions with humanity post-Fall. Some traditions link this to corruption of the Adamic image.

entities.research_notes: Adam occupies a unique position as both the historical progenitor of all humanity and the theological type that makes Christ's work comprehensible. Paul's use of the Adam-Christ contrast (Romans 5, 1 Corinthians 15) is one of the most structurally sophisticated arguments in the New Testament — two representative heads, one of ruin, one of restoration. Kabbalistic tradition develops Adam Kadmon as the cosmic template preceding creation itself.

genealogy.lineage: Ruth 4:18–22: Perez → Hezron → Ram → Amminadab → Nahshon → Salmon → Boaz → Obed → Jesse → David
genealogy.to_christ: Matthew 1:6–16: David → Solomon → ... → Joseph (legal father of Jesus). Luke 3:31–32: David → Nathan → ... → Mary's line. The Davidic covenant (2 Samuel 7:12–16) promised David an eternal dynasty — fulfilled in Christ.

biblical_angel.name: David
biblical_angel.canonical_function: Second king of unified Israel; established Jerusalem as capital; received the covenant promise of an eternal dynasty (2 Samuel 7:12–16); author of many Psalms; ancestor of the Messiah
source_texts: Acts 2:29–31 (Peter's Pentecost sermon on David and resurrection)
Zohar — David as the earthly king corresponding to the divine Kingdom (Malkuth)

islamic.quranic_reference: Quran 4:163; 17:55 (given the Psalms/Zabur); 21:78–80; 27:15–16 (granted wisdom and speech of birds)
islamic.isra_iliyyat_link: Dāwūd receives the Zabur (Psalms) as divine scripture; governs justly; prefigures Suleiman (Solomon). Islamic tradition emphasizes his repentance and musical worship.

functional_domains: Royal Ancestor of Christ (Son of David)

relationships.source_text: Matthew 1:1 — 'The genealogy of Jesus the Messiah, the son of David, the son of Abraham'; Luke 1:32 'He will be great and will be called the Son of the Most High... the throne of David his father'
relationships.notes: The most direct genealogical connection in the database. The Davidic covenant of 2 Samuel 7 is fulfilled in Christ. Jesus is called 'Son of David' 16 times in the Gospels — the most common messianic title used to address him.

relationships.source_text: Luke 3:31–38 traces the line from Jesus → David → Jesse → ... → Seth → Adam → God
relationships.notes: The Lucan genealogy makes the full chain explicit, grounding the Incarnation in all of human history from first man to Messiah.

entities.research_notes: David's theological importance in this concordance is primarily genealogical and typological: the Davidic covenant guarantees that the Messiah would be of his lineage (royal), and multiple psalms attributed to David (especially 22 and 110) are read in the New Testament as messianic prophecy. The connection between David-as-shepherd-king and Christ-as-Good-Shepherd (John 10) is among the richest typological threads in Christian scripture.

genealogy.lineage: Genesis 5:18–24: Seth → Enosh → Kenan → Mahalalel → Jared → Enoch → Methuselah → Lamech → Noah
genealogy.to_christ: Luke 3:37 includes Enoch in the genealogical chain from Jesus to Adam

biblical_angel.name: Enoch
biblical_angel.canonical_function: Seventh generation from Adam; 'walked faithfully with God; then he was no more, because God took him away' (Genesis 5:24) — one of two men in Scripture not to die. Father of Methuselah. Jude 14–15 quotes his prophecy about the Lord's return.
source_texts: Hebrews 11:5 (by faith Enoch was taken from this life)
Jude 1:14–15 (Enoch prophesied about the Second Coming)

enochian.name: Enoch
enochian.sin_or_role: Righteous patriarch taken up to heaven; receives cosmic visions and tours; given knowledge of the Watchers, celestial mechanics, and eschatology; intercedes for the fallen Watchers (unsuccessfully); becomes scribe of divine judgment
enochian.chapter_reference: 1 Enoch 1–36 (Book of Watchers); 37–71 (Similitudes — Enoch identified with Son of Man)

islamic.isra_iliyyat_link: Classical Islamic scholars (al-Tabari, al-Tha'labi) identify Idris with Enoch; credited with introducing writing, astronomy, and tailoring. Raised to a 'high station' — widely interpreted as translation without death.

relationships.source_text: 3 Enoch 3–15 — 'I am Enoch the son of Jared... the Holy One took me from their midst to be a witness to the world'
relationships.notes: The transformation of the patriarch Enoch into the angel Metatron is the central event of 3 Enoch. This represents the most theologically significant human-to-angel transformation in Jewish mysticism.

relationships.source_text: Agrippa OCPhil III; Renaissance syncretic sources
relationships.notes: Both Enoch and Hermes Trismegistus represent the archetype of the human sage translated to divine status as celestial scribe. Islamic identification of Idris-as-Enoch with Hermes strengthens this comparison.

Enoch is in the direct ancestral line of Jesus per Luke 3. His translation without death also provides a typological anticipation of the Resurrection and Ascension — the righteous body taken up into God's presence.

entities.research_notes: Enoch is the most cross-traditional figure in the entire database after Jesus: he appears in the canonical Bible, the pseudepigraphical 1 Enoch (used as Scripture by Jude), the Kabbalistic 3 Enoch, and the Quran as Idris. The Similitudes of Enoch (1 Enoch 37–71) use the phrase 'Son of Man' in a messianic context — the same title Jesus uses of himself in the Gospels, and scholars debate whether Jesus was consciously referencing 1 Enoch.

genealogy.lineage: Genesis 5: Adam → Seth → Enosh → Kenan → Mahalalel → Jared → Enoch → Methuselah → Lamech → Noah
genealogy.to_christ: Luke 3:36 — Jesus' genealogy runs through Shem, son of Noah → ... → David → Jesus

biblical_angel.name: Noah
biblical_angel.canonical_function: Tenth generation from Adam; righteous man in corrupt generation; commanded to build the Ark; survivor of the Flood through which God judged and renewed creation; received Noahic Covenant (rainbow, Genesis 9:8–17); father of Shem, Ham, Japheth — ancestors of all post-diluvian nations
source_texts: Matthew 24:37–38 (days of Noah as eschatological type)

enochian.name: Noah
enochian.sin_or_role: Son of Lamech; his exceptional whiteness and luminous eyes at birth led his father to fear he was a Watcher's son — Enoch reassures Lamech of Noah's true parentage. Noah survives the Flood judgment that destroys the Nephilim.
enochian.chapter_reference: 1 Enoch 106–107 (Birth of Noah); Book of Giants (4Q530)

islamic.isra_iliyyat_link: Nuh preaches for 950 years (Quran 29:14); his son's refusal to board the Ark is treated at length; the Flood establishes divine judgment and mercy as theological constants. Second most frequently mentioned prophet in the Quran after Moses.

functional_domains: New Beginning / Second Adam of Post-Diluvian World
Type of Salvation Through Baptism (1 Peter 3)

relationships.notes: Peter explicitly reads Noah and the Ark as a type (typos) of baptism and salvation. Jesus uses the 'days of Noah' as a prophetic parallel to conditions preceding his return. The Ark as vessel of salvation through water maps typologically onto baptism, the sacrament of entry into the new covenant community.

Noah is the great-grandson of Enoch (Enoch → Methuselah → Lamech → Noah). Enoch was translated before the Flood; Noah survived through it — both escape the judgment of their generation through divine favor.

entities.research_notes: Noah's theological function in this concordance is primarily typological and genealogical. He is the hinge between the antediluvian world (Adam through Enoch) and the post-diluvian world from which all current nations and the Abrahamic lineage derive. Jesus' genealogy passes through Shem, establishing continuity of the chosen line through the Flood event.

genealogy.lineage: Genesis 11: Shem → Arpachshad → Shelah → Eber → Peleg → Reu → Serug → Nahor → Terah → Abram/Abraham
genealogy.to_christ: Matthew 1:1–2: 'The genealogy of Jesus the Messiah, the son of David, the son of Abraham: Abraham was the father of Isaac, Isaac the father of Jacob...' Christ's genealogy begins here in Matthew.

biblical_angel.name: Abraham
biblical_angel.canonical_function: Recipient of the Abrahamic Covenant (Genesis 12, 15, 17, 22); promised that through his seed all nations would be blessed (Genesis 12:3) — fulfilled in Christ (Galatians 3:16); father of Isaac through Sarah; father of Ishmael through Hagar; justified by faith not works (Genesis 15:6; Romans 4; Galatians 3); offered Isaac on Moriah — typological of the Father offering the Son
source_texts: Galatians 3:6–29 (the promise to Abraham's seed fulfilled in Christ)
John 8:56 (Abraham saw Christ's day and rejoiced)
Zohar — Abraham corresponds to the sephira Chesed (loving-kindness), the attribute he exemplified

islamic.quranic_reference: Quran 2:124–132; 3:65–68; 4:125 (Friend of God — Khalīl Allāh); Surah 14 (Ibrahim); 6:74–83
islamic.isra_iliyyat_link: Ibrāhīm is 'Friend of God' (Khalīl Allāh) and is considered a Hanif — a primordial monotheist before either Judaism or Islam as formal religions. He and Ishmael rebuild the Kaaba (2:127). The Quran claims the true religion of Ibrahim as the essence of Islam.

functional_domains: Justified by Faith — Theological Foundation of Paul's Soteriology
Typological Prefiguration of the Father-Son Sacrifice (Akedah / Moriah)

relationships.source_text: Matthew 1:1–2; Galatians 3:16 — 'The promises were spoken to Abraham and to his seed... meaning one person, who is Christ'
relationships.notes: Paul's argument in Galatians 3 makes the Abrahamic covenant explicitly about Christ: the singular 'seed' promised to Abraham is Christ himself. Matthew opens his entire Gospel by establishing Jesus as 'Son of Abraham,' rooting the Incarnation in covenant history.

relationships.source_text: Matthew 1:2–6 — Abraham → Isaac → Jacob → Judah → ... → Jesse → David
relationships.notes: The genealogical chain from Abraham to David is eleven generations in Matthew 1. Both figures are covenant recipients — Abrahamic covenant of blessing to all nations, Davidic covenant of eternal throne — and both point toward their fulfillment in Christ.

entities.research_notes: Abraham is the genealogical and theological pivot of the entire Abrahamic tradition. The three monotheistic world religions — Judaism, Christianity, Islam — all trace their theological identity through him, making him the most historically consequential figure in the database after Jesus Christ. Paul's use of Abraham (Romans 4, Galatians 3) to argue that justification by faith predates the Mosaic law is one of the most structurally significant theological arguments in Christian thought. The Akedah (binding of Isaac) is interpreted in Christian typology as the most direct Old Testament prefiguration of Golgotha.

relationships.notes: Enlil is descended from / subordinate to Anu in most Sumerian genealogical schemes.

entities.research_notes: Supreme sky-god and father of the Anunnaki in Sumerian cosmogony; head of the divine assembly. His worship center was Uruk.

relationships.notes: Enlil is placed beneath Anu in the standard Sumerian divine hierarchy.

entities.research_notes: Executive deity who grants kingship and decrees fates; his flood decision in Atrahasis parallels Genesis 6.

relationships.notes: Enki is placed among the older divine generation beneath Anu/Enlil.

entities.research_notes: Trickster-sage who repeatedly saves humanity from the divine council's wrath; warned Utnapishtim/Atrahasis of the Flood.

relationships.notes: Inanna descends to Ereshkigal's realm; the two sisters represent complementary aspects of feminine divine power.

entities.research_notes: Most extensively hymned Sumerian goddess; her descent narrative influenced dying-and-rising deity scholarship.

relationships.notes: Ereshkigal and Inanna represent upper and lower world; life and death as complementary divine domains.

entities.research_notes: Underworld queen whose domain Inanna must strip herself to enter. Parallel to Persephone/Hades dynamic.

relationships.notes: Marduk is son of Enki/Ea in the Babylonian cosmic genealogy.

entities.research_notes: Slays Tiamat (primordial chaos) and creates the world from her body — the most explicit cosmogony-through-conquest in ancient Near East.

relationships.source_text: Book of the Dead; New Kingdom solar theology
relationships.notes: Ra and Osiris merge at midnight in New Kingdom solar theology as the unified sun-below-the-earth.

entities.research_notes: Principal solar deity; fused with Amun as Amun-Ra in Theban theology. Regenerates nightly through the Duat.

relationships.notes: Set and Horus represent the eternal conflict between chaos and order, usurpation and legitimate kingship, desert and fertile land.

entities.research_notes: Complex deity: in some periods protects Ra's sun boat against Apophis; in others embodies Seth as chaos-principle. His cult was suppressed and revived multiple times across Egyptian history.
